answer: Each identity must seal a unique piece of data and periodically prove it still holds a distinct copy, so one operator with a thousand identities must store a thousand genuinely different sealed sectors rather than pointing the same cheap disk at a thousand names. Each head pays its own cost, paid in full, since the cost is per identity. The kernel is the sealed sector, the nadir the replication challenge that proves it is still unique, and the vault the identity the sealed data is bound to; cloning the kernel fails the nadir, and one sector cannot satisfy two vault bindings.
